subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-18T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist & next steps

Hi Alex — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from the demo and our recommended next steps for the evaluation run:

1) Recommended model shortlist (based on your target UX: sub-200ms median LLM latency for short prompts, 95th pct < 400ms, and high factuality for product Q&A):
   - redwood-13b-q4_0 (balanced): best cost/quality tradeoff for retrieval-augmented Q&A; ~40-60ms token latency on dedicated T4-like instance at 8k context, estimated cost ~$0.08/1k tokens.
   - redwood-7b-v2 (low-latency): very low latency for interactive suggestions, good for completion-heavy flows; ~20-30ms token latency, estimated cost ~$0.035/1k tokens.
   - open-13b-chat-q8 (high-quality variant): stronger on tricky multi-step reasoning and edge-case product descriptions, higher cost and latency (~60-90ms token latency), estimated cost ~$0.12/1k tokens.

2) Why these three: each maps to a clear tradeoff frontier — 7B for latency/cost-sensitive widgets, 13B-q4 for balanced production rollout, open-13B-chat for higher-quality responses on complex queries.

3) Deliverables we attached: prompt set (acme_prompt_sets_v1.xlsx) with 120 representative prompts from your demo, benchmark report (acme_benchmark_report_20260218.pdf) with preliminary throughput/latency numbers from our internal run, and a gated mutual action plan (MAP) draft.

4) Proposed next steps:
   - You confirm 1-2 priority flows (e.g., product Q&A + recommendations) we should focus our evaluation on.
   - We run a short production-style eval (1k-2k queries) across the three models and share token-level latency/cost breakdown + quality metrics (helpfulness, factuality, hallucination rate). Rafael to scope the run.
   - Joint sync next week to review results and pick a rollout plan (canary on dedicated pool or hosted API).

Please let me know which flows you want prioritized and whether the MAP timeline looks OK. Happy to set up the evaluation window this week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Thanks Marissa — great summary and helpful to see the three buckets. A few quick clarifying questions before we lock the flows:

- For "product Q&A" we expect ~60% of queries to be short factual lookups (sku, price, availability), and ~40% longer multi-turn clarifications (recommendations, substitutions). Which model do you expect to be the best first-cut for hybrid workload?
- For the evaluation run, can you also include example prompts from the attachment mapped to the flows (so our SRE and privacy folks can reproduce)?

Also — Rafael/Monica: any security or data-retention constraints we should flag before the eval? We need to ensure PII is stripped for the test dataset.

If it helps, we can prioritize product Q&A + recommendations for the first run.

—Alex
Director, Product AI — Acme Retail
alex.johnson@acme-retail.com

Thanks Alex — that priority makes sense. Quick answers inline and next steps:

- Hybrid workload recommendation: start with redwood-13b-q4_0 as the baseline for both short factual lookups and multi-turn clarifications. It hits the best balance and supports our strongest canonical retrieval augmentation paths. redwood-7b-v2 can be used as a low-latency fallback for UI widgets (typeahead, inline suggestions). open-13b-chat-q8 reserved for the long-tail complex queries where precision is paramount.

- I've added a mapping tab to acme_prompt_sets_v1.xlsx called "MAP_FLOW_MAPPINGS" that assigns each prompt to either PRODUCT_QA or RECOMMENDATIONS and notes whether the prompt contains PII. Please use that for the SRE/privacy reproduce run.

- Rafael: for the eval dataset we will mark PII fields and provide a redacted dataset. Monica, can you confirm redaction pipeline and retention window (we recommend 7 days for the ephemeral eval bucket)?

Next steps: Rafael will scope the 2k-query eval (runs across the three models), and we'll share a short results deck by EOW. If the numbers are aligned with your SLOs we'll propose a 2-week canary on Dedicated.

Thanks — will kick off the eval once Rafael confirms infra.

Best,
Marissa

Alex/Marissa — I'll scope the eval today. Plan below and a couple of operational notes:

Planned eval scope:
- 2,000 queries split: 1,200 PRODUCT_QA (mix of short lookups and multi-turn followups), 800 RECOMMENDATIONS.
- Runs: redwood-7b-v2, redwood-13b-q4_0, open-13b-chat-q8.
- Metrics: median + 95th latency (ms), tokens per inference, cost per 1k tokens estimate, helpfulness (1-5) and factuality/hallucination flags.
- Timebox: 24-hour run on a dedicated test pool; results deck by 2026-02-20 EOD PT.

Operational notes / risks:
- Quantized models (q4/q8) can sometimes show subtle quality regressions on rare edge cases. We'll include a focused prompt set of 75 "regression candidates" (high-precision product descriptions) so you can see where differences show up.
- Monica: for the ephemeral eval bucket we recommend retention=7 days and auto-delete. Please confirm pipeline (PII redaction + workspace access list).

David: can you run the latency microbench for the redwood-13b-q4_0 on the dedicated instance we proposed and share the raw perf logs? We'll attach to the deck.

I'll schedule the run for Friday (2026-02-20) morning PT unless you request otherwise.

-Rafael
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
